title: Number of Closed Islands
summary: Determine the count of islands in a 2D grid that are completely surrounded by water, where an island is defined as a group of connected 0s (land) and a closed island is one that is fully enclosed by 1s (water) on all sides.
statement: Determine the count of islands in a 2D grid that are completely surrounded by water, where an island is defined as a group of connected 0s (land) and a closed island is one that is fully enclosed by 1s (water) on all sides.
constraints: Zero is land and one is water.
A land component is closed when it is surrounded by water and never touches the grid boundary.
Return the number of four-connected closed land components.
hints: Crossing the grid boundary makes that component open; water contributes no opening.
Combine all four recursive directions while still evaluating every branch.
A component is closed exactly when none of its reachable land paths exits the grid.
editorial: A component is closed exactly when none of its reachable land paths exits the grid.

tests.explanation: Two interior land components do not touch the boundary.
Every land component reaches an outer edge, so none is closed.
